THIS WRIT PETITION (CIVIL) HAVING BEEN FINALLY HEARD ON 19.12.2025, ALONG WITH WP(C).16774/2022 AND CONNECTED CASES, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 WP(C) Nos.18468 & 16774 of 2022 and 9767 & 9610 of 2025  -9-  2025:KER:98653  JUDGMENT Dated this the 19th day of December, 2025 Since a common issue is involved in these writ petitions,
they are heard and disposed of by a common judgment.

2. WP(C) No.16774 of 2022 is filed by a person who has developed ailments after having food from the hotel run by the 4 th respondent in the name and style 'Al-Raidan Family Restaurant and Saudi Kuzhimanthi'.

Petitioner would contend that in Ext.P5 order there is a finding by the Municipality that the hotel is being run without getting any license from the Municipality, and that contaminated water is being flown into public place, and a direction was issued to the 4th respondent to shut down the hotel within 48 hours.
Petitioner would contend that it is due to the influence of the 3rd respondent, Chairman of the Pattambi Municipality, that no further action was taken in the matter.
It is aggrieved by the same that the petitioner has approached this Court seeking implementation of Ext.P5 order.

3. The 4th respondent filed a detailed counter affidavit, wherein it is contended that the restaurant had been running from 2002 onwards after obtaining license from the Pattambi Municipality, and the license was issued in the name of another partner of the firm, Mr.Abdul Sathar.
It is contended that license WP(C) Nos.18468 & 16774 of 2022 and 9767 & 9610 of 2025 2025:KER:98653 was issued till 2017-18.

It is further submitted that the 5 th respondent landlord was trying to evict the 4 th respondent from the said premises, and the present writ petition is one filed to achieve the said intention of the 5th respondent.
The 5th respondent would submit that the restaurant was closed for some time in the year 2020-21 due to the covid pandemic.
Thereafter, an application for renewal of license was submitted which was received by the respondent Municipality as evident from Ext.R4(f).

A.K.G. Devadas vs Pattambi Municipality on 19 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182371067/
6

Based on a complaint filed by the landlord contending that no consent has been obtained for renewing the license, Ext.R4(g) proceedings were initiated directing the 4th respondent to close down the business, against which WP(C) No.18464 of 2022 was filed, wherein Ext.R4(h) interim order was passed.

Petitioner submits that based on the judgment of the Apex Court in Sudhakaran v.
Corporation of Trivandrum and Another [2016 (3) KHC 803], consent of the landlord is not at all required so long as the tenancy is prevailing.

sentences.text: 4. WP(C) No.18468 of 2022 is filed by the owner of the hotel challenging Ext.P7 order, wherein the petitioner was directed to close down the hotel since no consent has been obtained from the landlord.

Petitioner would contend that he along with other partners were conducting a restaurant at Pattambi and have WP(C) Nos.18468 & 16774 of 2022 and 9767 & 9610 of 2025 2025:KER:98653 obtained license from then Pattambi Grama Panchayat in the year 2002, and later the partnership deed was reconstituted as per Ext.P1 and going by Ext.P1, application for license could be applied in the name of any of the partner for and on behalf of the firm and that shall be the property of the firm.
That is how Ext.P2 license was issued in the name of Mr.Abdul Sathar.

The restaurant was run after obtaining necessary license and clearances, but due to the outbreak of Covid-19, the restaurant was closed down for some time, and later by Ext.P6 the application for renewal of license was submitted on 21.04.2022.

Along with the same, a consent letter of the owner of the building was also produced and since there was some dispute between the petitioner and the landlord, an objection was made by the landlord before the Municipality that the landlord has not given consent and the consent letter produced by the petitioner is a forged one.
Thereupon Ext.P7 communication was issued directing the petitioner to close down the business.

5. Petitioner relying on the judgment in Sudhakaran's case cited supra submits that, since it is a case of renewal of license, no fresh consent from the landlord is required, and therefore the issuance of Ext.P7 is absolutely without any basis.

The landlord who got impleaded as additional 3 rd respondent submits that, earlier one Abdul Sathar obtained a license from the WP(C) Nos.18468 &
16774 of 2022 and 9767 & 9610 of 2025 2025:KER:98653 1st respondent Municipality for running a hotel by the name 'Malabar Spicy Hotel' and the said hotel was run by the aforesaid licensee till 2019, and the same was cancelled based on an application submitted by Abdul Sathar as evident from Ext.R3(a) communication received as per the provisions of the Right to Information Act.

After cancellation, the petitioner is running a hotel under the name and style 'Saudi Kuzhimanthi' in the room which is allotted to Mr.Abdul Sathar without obtaining any license from the 2nd respondent.

The additional 3rd respondent would further submit that the registration certificate of the Food and Safety Department evident by Ext.P2 is issued in respect of 'Malabar Spicy Restaurant', whereas Ext.P4 registration certificate is issued in favour of 'Saudi Kuzhimandi Restaurant'.

The petitioner had gone to the extent of creating a forged consent letter produced as Ext.R2(e) and submitted along with an application for obtaining D&O license from the Municipality which is not even notarised and the address of the witnesses are also not revealed.

Thereupon complaint was preferred before the respondent Municipality requesting not to issue any license to the petitioner and to take stringent action against the petitioner for producing a forged document.

On the basis of the complaint a hearing was conducted, and after the hearing Ext.P7 order was issued directing the WP(C) Nos.18468 & 16774 of 2022 and 9767 & 9610 of 2025 2025:KER:98653 petitioner to close down the hotel.

Going by Ext.R3(d) communication issued by the Municipality, appropriate steps A.K.G. Devadas vs Pattambi Municipality on 19 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182371067/
7 have been taken by the Municipality before the Police authorities to initiate action against the petitioner.

6. A detailed counter affidavit has been filed by the respondent Municipality, wherein it is reiterated that the petitioner has submitted a fresh application for license along with a consent letter of the landlord as Ext.R1(a).
A hearing was conducted by the Secretary of the Municipality and the landlord denied the consent letter and alleged that the letter is a forged one and cannot be accepted.
Thereupon as per Ext.R1(d) communication, Secretary of the Municipality has forwarded the same to the Station House Officer for taking appropriate action.

It is further submitted that the license originally issued for the hotel by name 'Malabar Spicy' functioning in the same place was cancelled on the request of Abdul Sathar, the license holder during the year 2019 itself, and therefore the hotel is now running without any license, and therefore proceedings were initiated as per Ext.P7 for closing down the restaurant.

Pursuant to the direction issued by this Court, the D&O license register and a report was produced by the learned Counsel appearing for the Municipality along with a memo, wherein it is categorically stated that the license issued in the name of WP(C) Nos.18468 &
16774 of 2022 and 9767 & 9610 of 2025 2025:KER:98653 Abdul Sathar for running a restaurant by name 'Malabar Spicy Hotel' has been cancelled based on an application from Mr.Abdul Sathar as per order referred to as H1/4330/19 dated 28.03.2019.

7. WP(C) No.9610 of 2025 is filed by the landlord mainly contending that the 5th respondent who is the petitioner in WP(C) No.18468 of 2022 is attempting to obtain a new electric connection in the building No.21/1275 of Pattambi Municipality without obtaining written consent of the 2nd petitioner who is the owner of the building, and relying on Regulation 45 of the Electricity Supply Code 2014, it is contended that for getting electric connection for the licensee, certain documents including copy of the title deed or lease agreement has to be produced.

Regulation 45(2) mandates that if the applicant is not an owner but occupier of the premises, he shall furnish an NOC from the owner of the premises along with one of the documents mentioned in Regulation 45.

Since an attempt is made to obtain an electricity connection in building No.21/1275 of Pattambi Municipality without obtaining NOC from the 2nd petitioner that the present writ petition has been filed commanding the respondents 1 to 4 not to effect any electricity connection to building No.21/1275 of Pattambi Municipality owned by the 2nd petitioner without the written consent of the 2nd petitioner.

WP(C) Nos.18468 & 16774 of 2022 and 9767 & 9610 of 2025 2025:KER:98653 8. WP(C) No.9767 of 2025 is filed by the owner of the restaurant contending that attempts are made to disconnect the electricity connection due to the objection raised by the landlord, and without notice electricity connection of the premises was disconnected by the 3rd respondent on 08.03.2025.
Petitioner submits that the attempt to disconnect the electricity connection is only a short cut method to evict the petitioner.
It is seen that when the matter came up for consideration on 14.03.2025, this Court has directed the power supply to the premises of the petitioner to be reconnected forthwith.
9. I have heard the rival contentions on both sides.

A.K.G. Devadas vs Pattambi Municipality on 19 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182371067/
8 10.

The specific contention raised by the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner in WP(C)
No.18468 of 2022 is that the restaurant was functioning in the tenanted premises of the additional 3rd respondent from 2002 onwards, and going by Ext.P1 reconstituted partnership firm, if license or registration is taken by any of the partners of the firm in his individual name for and on behalf of the firm, then that shall be the property of the firm.

Based on the same, it is contended that at that point of time license was obtained by one Abdul Sathar who is one of the partners, and therefore the said license taken by Abdul Sathar is for and on behalf of the firm, and therefore the said license granted still WP(C) Nos.18468 & 16774 of 2022 and 9767 & 9610 of 2025 2025:KER:98653 continues, and that the petitioner is entitled for renewal of the same.
The license have been renewed upto 2017, as evident from Ext.P3, but in the name of Abdul Sathar and the name of the restaurant is 'Hotel Malabar Spicy'.
It is admitted that for a short period during covid, the restaurant was closed down, and thereafter Ext.P6 application was submitted for renewal of license.
As part of the enquiry a hearing was conducted and the landlord objected to the grant of the license stating that he has not given consent, and consent if any produced is a forged one.
Based on the same, Ext.P7 communication was issued directing the petitioner to close down the restaurant as no license has been obtained by the petitioner.

11. Specific contention raised by the petitioner is based on Sudhakaran's case cited supra, wherein the Court has held that once consent is given by the landlord and the tenancy is subsisting, there is no requirement of NOC from the landlord when that person applies for renewal of license or apply for license after the expiry of the period of the existing license.
Petitioner also relies on Section 492 of the Kerala Municipality Act, 1994 (for short, 'Act 1994') which contains some general provisions regarding license and permission.

Based on the same, it is the contention of the petitioner that even the consent from the landlord is not required WP(C) Nos.18468 & 16774 of 2022 and 9767 & 9610 of 2025 2025:KER:98653 since this is a case of renewal of license and even if the landlord takes the contention that the consent granted is a forged one, the same need not be looked into inasmuch as consent from the landlord is not required for renewal of the license as held by the Apex Court in Sudhakaran's case cited supra as well as the judgment of this Court in Shajahan M.I. v. Alice George and Others [2015 (1) KHC 811].

sentences.text: Whereas the consistent case of the landlord in this case is that the restaurant was earlier run by Mr.Abdul Sathar in the name and style 'Malabar Spicy Hotel' and the aforesaid license was till 2019 and was cancelled as per application dated 28.03.2019 as evident from Ext.R3(a) and thereafter the petitioner has submitted a fresh application for obtaining D&O license from the Municipality along with Ext.R3(b) consent letter issued by the landlord which is alleged to be a fraudulently created document.

The decisions relied on by the petitioner in support of his contention can have no application in the facts and circumstances of the case, inasmuch as those decisions were dealing with renewal of license originally granted.
But the present case is one case where the original licensee has cancelled the license and is a case of fresh issuance of a D&O license for running a restaurant in a different name.

When the application for D&O license was submitted by the petitioner, a WP(C) Nos.18468 & 16774 of 2022 and 9767 & 9610 of 2025 2025:KER:98653 hearing was conducted and the 3rd respondent landlord, took a contention that the consent letter produced along with the application is a forged one, and therefore Ext.P7 order was issued directing to close down the functioning of the restaurant which is running without obtaining a license.

A.K.G. Devadas vs Pattambi Municipality on 19 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182371067/
9 12.

It is seen that at the request of the 3 rd respondent, proceedings have been initiated for forwarding the complaint to the police for detailed investigation in the matter regarding submission of the forged consent letter.

Going by the counter affidavit filed by the respondent Municipality he had admitted that the license issued in favour of Abdul Sathar for running a restaurant by name 'Malabar Spicy' was cancelled during 2019 itself, and thereafter the hotel is running without any license, and that since a dispute was raised that the consent letter produced is a forged one, the matter was referred to the police as evident from Ext.R1(d) communication issued by the Secretary of the Municipality.

To substantiate that, the license originally issued in the name of Abdul Sathar for running a restaurant by name 'Malabar Spicy Hotel', is cancelled, the extract of the D&O demand register of the Municipality is produced which reveal that the license has been cancelled based on the application submitted by Abdul Sathar.
It is in the said background, the issue raised by the petitioner and the respondent WP(C) Nos.18468 & 16774 of 2022 and 9767 & 9610 of 2025 2025:KER:98653 is to be considered.
Section 492 of the Act, 1994 deals with general provisions regarding license and permission.

Section 492(1) to (4) which is relevant for consideration of this case reads as follows:-
"492. GENERAL PROVISIONS REGARDING LICENCES AND PERMISSIONS.-- (1)
Every licence and permission granted under this Act or any rule or bye-law made thereunder shall specify the period, if any, for which, and the restrictions, limitations and conditions, subject to which, the same is granted and shall be signed by the Secretary.

(2) Every licence issued by the Secretary shall specify the person to whom,
the premises in respect of which, and the trade or business or undertaking for which the licence is granted and for any change in the person, the premises or the business,
trade, or undertaking, a fresh licence or permission shall betaken with or without payment of further fee as the Municipality may fix.

(3) Where any person intending to obtain a licence or permission for the first time and where the applicant is a person other than the owner of the premises in question,
he shall, along with the application produce the written consent of the owner of the premises and the period of the licence shall not exceed the period, if any, specified in the consent.

(4) Where the applicant seeking renewal of a licence or permission in respect of the trade or business licensed in the premises mentioned in sub-section (3)
is a person different from the original licensee or not the legal heir of the original license the consent of the owner shall be required."

So going by Section 492(3), when any person intending to obtain a license or permission for the first time and whether the applicant is WP(C) Nos.18468 & 16774 of 2022 and 9767 & 9610 of 2025 2025:KER:98653 a person other than the owner of the premises in question, he shall along with the application, produce the written consent of the owner of the premises and the period of license shall not exceed the period if any specified in the consent.

Whereas, Section 492(4) mandates that, where the applicant seeks renewal of license or permission in respect of the trade or business, licensed in the premises mentioned in Sub-section (3) is a person different from the original licensee or not the legal heir of the original licensee the consent of the land owner shall be required.

So going by the mandate of the Section, when it is the case of renewal and the application submitted is not by the A.K.G. Devadas vs Pattambi Municipality on 19 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182371067/
10 original licensee or its legal heirs, then naturally consent of the landlord is to be obtained.

sentences.text: 13. In Sudhakaran's case cited supra, the Apex Court was considering a case of a renewal of license by the original licensee himself and held that in case of a renewal of the original license no consent from the landlord is required.

This Court in Shajahan's case cited supra was also considering a similar circumstance, wherein the landlord took a contention that the consent letter produced along with the application for renewal of license is a forged one.

Court held that since in a case of renewal of license by the original licensee himself no consent letter is to be obtained from the landlord, the contention of the landlord that the consent WP(C) Nos.18468 & 16774 of 2022 and 9767 & 9610 of 2025 2025:KER:98653 granted is a forged one is not at all material for grant of renewal of license because application for renewal of license is submitted by the original licensee.
But the facts of this case is quite different from the facts dealt with by the Apex Court and this Court in the judgments cited supra.

Admittedly, the original licensee Abdul Sathar has submitted an application for cancellation of the license and the same was cancelled as per order dated 28.03.2019, and the same is reflected in the D&O demand register produced by the Municipality along with a memo.

Therefore, the application submitted by the petitioner is not a case of renewal of license, it can only be for issuance of a fresh license for which consent of the landlord is mandatory going by Section 492 of the Act, 1994, inasmuch as the application is filed not by a person who is the original license holder.

When such an application was filed, the Municipality has called for a hearing, wherein the landlord has taken a contention that the consent letter produced by the petitioner is a forged one,
and relying on the same, the Municipality has issued Ext.P7 communication produced in WP(C)
No.18468 of 2022 holding that the petitioner is running the restaurant without obtaining necessary license in this regard.

It is also to be seen that the Secretary of the Municipality has as per Ext.R1(d)
has forwarded the matter for necessary enquiry by the WP(C) Nos.18468 & 16774 of 2022 and 9767 & 9610 of 2025 2025:KER:98653 Police authorities since the landlord has raised a contention that the consent letter produced along with the application for issuance of a D&O license is a forged one.
14.
In the above facts and circumstances of the case, I am of the view that the application for D&O license should be supported by a consent letter or a 'No Objection Certificate' issued by the landlord.

When the landlord in the hearing conducted by the Secretary of the Municipality categorically takes a stand that the consent granted is a forged one, the Municipality cannot be found at fault in not granting a D&O license to the petitioner as requested by him.

It is also to be seen that since a complaint has been raised by the landlord that the consent letter obtained is a forged one, the matter has been referred to the Police authorities for appropriate action.
In view of the above facts and circumstances, I find no reason to interfere with Ext.P7 notice issued by the respondent Municipality produced in WP(C) No.18468 of 2022.

Accordingly above writ petitions are disposed of as follows:-
1. WP(C) No.18468 of 2022 and WP(C) No.9767 of 2025 are accordingly dismissed.

opennyai_summary.facts:
A.K.G. Devadas vs Pattambi Municipality on 19 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182371067/
6
The restaurant was run after obtaining necessary license and clearances, but due to the outbreak of Covid-19, the restaurant was closed down for some time, and later by Ext.P6 the application for renewal of license was submitted on 21.04.2022.
Along with the same, a consent letter of the owner of the building was also produced and since there was some dispute between the petitioner and the landlord, an objection was made by the landlord before the Municipality that the landlord has not given consent and the consent letter produced by the petitioner is a forged one.
Thereupon Ext.P7 communication was issued directing the petitioner to close down the business.
Thereupon complaint was preferred before the respondent Municipality requesting not to issue any license to the petitioner and to take stringent action against the petitioner for producing a forged document.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
Petitioner submits that based on the judgment of the Apex Court in Sudhakaran v.
Corporation of Trivandrum and Another [2016 (3) KHC 803], consent of the landlord is not at all required so long as the tenancy is prevailing.
Based on the same, it is the contention of the petitioner that even the consent from the landlord is not required WP(C) Nos.18468 & 16774 of 2022 and 9767 & 9610 of 2025 2025:KER:98653 since this is a case of renewal of license and even if the landlord takes the contention that the consent granted is a forged one, the same need not be looked into inasmuch as consent from the landlord is not required for renewal of the license as held by the Apex Court in Sudhakaran's case cited supra as well as the judgment of this Court in Shajahan M.I. v. Alice George and Others [2015 (1) KHC 811].
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
But the present case is one case where the original licensee has cancelled the license and is a case of fresh issuance of a D&O license for running a restaurant in a different name.
When the application for D&O license was submitted by the petitioner, a WP(C) Nos.18468 & 16774 of 2022 and 9767 & 9610 of 2025 2025:KER:98653 hearing was conducted and the 3rd respondent landlord, took a contention that the consent letter produced along with the application is a forged one, and therefore Ext.P7 order was issued directing to close down the functioning of the restaurant which is running without obtaining a license.
A.K.G. Devadas vs Pattambi Municipality on 19 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182371067/
9 12.
Court held that since in a case of renewal of license by the original licensee himself no consent letter is to be obtained from the landlord, the contention of the landlord that the consent WP(C) Nos.18468 & 16774 of 2022 and 9767 & 9610 of 2025 2025:KER:98653 granted is a forged one is not at all material for grant of renewal of license because application for renewal of license is submitted by the original licensee.
Admittedly, the original licensee Abdul Sathar has submitted an application for cancellation of the license and the same was cancelled as per order dated 28.03.2019, and the same is reflected in the D&O demand register produced by the Municipality along with a memo.
Therefore, the application submitted by the petitioner is not a case of renewal of license, it can only be for issuance of a fresh license for which consent of the landlord is mandatory going by Section 492 of the Act, 1994, inasmuch as the application is filed not by a person who is the original license holder.
When such an application was filed, the Municipality has called for a hearing, wherein the landlord has taken a contention that the consent letter produced by the petitioner is a forged one,
and relying on the same, the Municipality has issued Ext.P7 communication produced in WP(C)
No.18468 of 2022 holding that the petitioner is running the restaurant without obtaining necessary license in this regard.
It is also to be seen that the Secretary of the Municipality has as per Ext.R1(d)
has forwarded the matter for necessary enquiry by the WP(C) Nos.18468 & 16774 of 2022 and 9767 & 9610 of 2025 2025:KER:98653 Police authorities since the landlord has raised a contention that the consent letter produced along with the application for issuance of a D&O license is a forged one.
14.
In the above facts and circumstances of the case, I am of the view that the application for D&O license should be supported by a consent letter or a 'No Objection Certificate' issued by the landlord.
When the landlord in the hearing conducted by the Secretary of the Municipality categorically takes a stand that the consent granted is a forged one, the Municipality cannot be found at fault in not granting a D&O license to the petitioner as requested by him.
It is also to be seen that since a complaint has been raised by the landlord that the consent letter obtained is a forged one, the matter has been referred to the Police authorities for appropriate action.
